readings.sections_read: p1 introductory correction discussion; pp4–5 context/cost; p9 credibility intervals; p10 local validity advice
readings.confirmed: Structured interviews retain a high mean validity, but the reported .42 mean has an80% credibility interval .18–.66 across settings. This is heterogeneity, not a95% confidence interval on the mean. Authors also discuss development time, cost and applicant context.
readings.limits: No numerical transfer to software recommendations or LLM procedures; this reinspection does not count as another method paper.

readings.sections_read: abstract; results atp4; Table1 atp5; discussion p6
readings.confirmed: In the ECG verification comparison, both conditions had89 interpretations; net errors corrected were26 with checklist and3 without. Verification took63 versus35 seconds and added more characters.
readings.limits: Fifteen experts and repeated ECG interpretation; improved error correction does not mean shorter output or lower elapsed time. Not a human review measurement in AF-RES-018.

readings.sections_read: objective/methods pp0–1; results p5; COMMENT p6
readings.confirmed: The antiplatelet recommendation example lagged cumulative evidence by10 years and the first published meta-analysis by6 years. The discussion identifies evidence volume, publication lag and differing endpoints as possible explanations.
readings.limits: Retrospective cumulative reconstruction and expert reviews were not randomized or matched in information/search budget. Different endpoints can explain some disagreement.

readings.confirmed: The paper distinguishes pairwise preference from individual scoring, and documents position/name bias on deliberately similar answers. Randomized labels alone are not a proof of invariant judgment.
readings.limits: These 2023 pairwise tests do not estimate bias in current individual software-candidate relevance labels.

readings.sections_read: Definition section2.1 and limitations5.2, PDF lines85–97 and490–521
readings.confirmed: Self-preference needs quality control; the authors distinguish capability-level causal evidence from the unproven claim that any particular example is preferred because it is recognized.
readings.limits: Summarization and fine-tuning experiments; same underlying generator for A/P means no automatic directional bias can be assumed.

readings.sections_read: Section3 experimental design and Table2, HTML lines121–156
readings.confirmed: Repeated trials, order changes and task/model variation distinguish stability from position consistency. Effects differ across judges and tasks.
readings.limits: The temperature and comparison settings differ from this workspace. One randomized order without reruns cannot identify a causal position effect here.

readings.confirmed: Length-controlled AlpacaEval estimates a regression-adjusted counterfactual with model, length and instruction terms. It is not produced by simply truncating text.
readings.limits: Our30-word normalization is a separate intervention and may remove qualifications; it does not inherit this estimator’s validation or remove all style bias.

readings.sections_read: Task C relevance definitions and annotation protocol, PDF lines326–426
readings.confirmed: The benchmark separates directly answering a subquestion from potentially useful context, employs at least three annotators and hidden checks, and reports an annotation-interface confusion between related and original questions.
readings.limits: Its Good/Bad merger is not our2/1/N/0 adoption codebook; human agreement there does not validate internal labels here.

readings.confirmed: The reference is the highest-voted eligible answer; additional valid-by-vote answers often exist. Retrieved supporting pages exclude Reddit itself.
readings.limits: Votes and reference selection do not establish actual adoption; this work is long-form explanatory QA rather than software deployment.

readings.confirmed: The methodological critique explains how system-order correlations and popularity-based pools can hide reversals for the strongest systems. Comparing similarity to an evaluator is not the same as validating user relevance.
readings.limits: This is an authored methodological argument and synthesis, not an institutional prohibition or a measured effect for the current model.

readings.confirmed: Incomplete relevance judgments and disappearance of documents are distinct problems. Fixed-depth precision has a different denominator and discrimination from recall-based measures.
readings.limits: The paper does not make a purposive software recommendation sample complete, nor justify replacing preregistered recall with a post hoc preferred metric.
